title: Chromium vs. Google Chrome
definition: Chromium is the open-source browser project and codebase; Google Chrome is a branded product assembled from Chromium plus Google-specific branding, distribution, services, and licensed components. When reading the tree, this distinction helps separate reusable browser machinery from product integrations.

title: Content Layer
definition: The content layer is Chromium's platform-neutral browser engine embedding API. It connects embedders such as Chrome to renderers, navigation, frames, processes, storage, and other web-facing machinery without defining Chrome's product UI.

title: Browser UI (Views)
definition: Views is Chromium's cross-platform desktop UI toolkit for browser chrome such as tabs, toolbars, dialogs, and menus. It builds a hierarchy of View objects, while platform styling and native widgets bridge that hierarchy to each operating system.

title: WebContents
definition: WebContents is the browser-side object representing the contents of a tab or other page container. It owns and coordinates navigation, the frame tree, renderer communication, and observers used by browser features.

title: WebUI
definition: WebUI is the framework behind internal pages such as chrome://settings, combining a privileged C++ controller with HTML, CSS, and TypeScript. Messages cross a deliberate binding layer so internal UI can call browser capabilities without exposing them to ordinary web pages.

title: Multi-process Architecture
definition: Chromium splits work across operating-system processes so a broken or compromised page does not automatically own the entire browser. The privileged browser process coordinates sandboxed renderers and specialized services such as GPU and network processes.

title: Browser Process
definition: The browser process is Chromium's trusted coordinator. It owns top-level UI and profiles, chooses renderer processes, brokers restricted resources, and validates requests arriving from less-trusted child processes.

title: Renderer Process
definition: A renderer process executes untrusted web content using Blink and V8. It is sandboxed and may host one or more related frames or workers, with placement constrained by SiteInstance and Site Isolation rules.

title: Frame Tree
definition: A page is represented as a tree of frames, beginning with a main frame and including every iframe. Because Site Isolation can place child frames in other processes, the logical frame tree spans process boundaries.

title: RenderFrameHost
definition: RenderFrameHost is the browser-side representation of a frame's current document and its connection to a renderer. Navigations can replace it, including with a host in another process, while the FrameTreeNode preserves the frame's stable position in the page.

title: SiteInstance
definition: A SiteInstance groups documents and workers that must be able to synchronously access one another and therefore must live together. Chromium uses it as a central unit when deciding renderer placement, process reuse, and isolation.

title: Site Isolation
definition: Site Isolation turns renderer processes into security boundaries between sites, including cross-site iframes. The browser enforces which site data a renderer may access and uses out-of-process frames plus process swaps to preserve web behavior.

title: Process Lock
definition: A ProcessLock records what site or origin a renderer process is allowed to host. Browser-side security checks consult that lock so a compromised renderer cannot simply request data belonging to another site.

title: Mojo IPC
definition: Mojo is Chromium's typed inter-process communication system. Interfaces declared in .mojom files generate bindings, letting components exchange messages over pipes while keeping process boundaries explicit.

title: Service & Utility Processes
definition: Chromium can package capabilities behind Mojo service interfaces and run them in dedicated or shared utility processes. This separates privileges, improves fault containment, and lets the browser choose an appropriate sandbox for each capability.

title: Navigation
definition: A navigation is the browser-controlled transition from a URL request to a committed document. Chromium coordinates redirects, security checks, response handling, renderer selection, and commit through a stateful NavigationRequest.

title: Navigation Throttle
definition: NavigationThrottle is an interception point where browser features may proceed, defer, cancel, or rewrite parts of a navigation. Throttles run at defined milestones, making policy and safety decisions composable without owning the entire navigation pipeline.

title: URLLoader
definition: URLLoader is the Mojo-facing abstraction used to perform URL requests and stream response metadata and bodies. URLLoaderFactory controls who may create loaders and carries request context across renderer, browser, and Network Service boundaries.

title: Network Service
definition: The Network Service owns most of Chromium's network stack behind Mojo interfaces and can run out of process. It performs requests while centralizing cookies, caches, proxy configuration, certificates, and transport policy away from sandboxed renderers.

title: Network Isolation Key
definition: A Network Isolation Key partitions network state according to the context that initiated a request. Partitioning caches and connections reduces cross-site information leaks and prevents one top-level site's activity from invisibly shaping another's network state.

title: HTTP Cache
definition: Chromium's HTTP cache stores reusable responses and validates them according to HTTP caching semantics. Its disk and memory backends sit beneath request jobs, and modern partitioning keys help prevent cache state from becoming a cross-site tracking channel.

title: Cookies
definition: Cookies are small pieces of site state attached to eligible HTTP requests and exposed through controlled web APIs. Chromium evaluates domain, path, security, SameSite, partitioning, and user-policy rules before reading or writing them.

title: Origin and Site
definition: An origin is the scheme, host, and port security principal used by the web platform; a site is a broader grouping usually based on scheme plus registrable domain. Chromium uses both, but for different boundaries such as same-origin access, process placement, cookies, and storage partitioning.

title: StoragePartition
definition: StoragePartition groups browser-managed storage and network state for a browsing context. It provides access to services such as cookies, service workers, DOM storage, and the network context, allowing embedders and privacy features to keep contexts separate.

title: Service Worker
definition: A service worker is an origin-bound background worker that can intercept fetches, serve cached responses, and handle events without an open page. Chromium coordinates its registration and lifetime in the browser while Blink runs its script in a renderer process.

title: Blink
definition: Blink is Chromium's rendering engine and web-platform implementation. It parses web content, exposes DOM APIs, runs document lifecycle phases, and produces paint artifacts that the compositor can turn into pixels.

title: DOM
definition: The Document Object Model is Blink's live object graph for a parsed document, including nodes, elements, text, and shadow trees. Script and parser mutations mark downstream style, layout, and paint work dirty rather than immediately drawing pixels.

title: Style Recalculation
definition: Style recalculation matches CSS rules and computes the resolved style used by each relevant DOM node. Blink tracks invalidation so changes can update affected subtrees instead of recomputing every element on every frame.

title: Layout
definition: Layout converts styled content into geometric boxes and fragments with sizes and positions. Modern Blink's LayoutNG algorithms produce immutable fragment output that later lifecycle stages use for hit testing and painting.

title: Document Lifecycle
definition: Blink advances a document through ordered lifecycle phases such as style, layout, pre-paint, and paint. Dirty-state tracking and phase ordering prevent later stages from consuming stale inputs and allow rendering work to be batched near a frame deadline.

title: Paint
definition: Paint walks layout output and records drawing instructions as display items grouped into paint chunks. It does not necessarily raster pixels immediately; it produces an efficient, reusable artifact for compositing and rasterization.

title: Paint Artifact
definition: A PaintArtifact is Blink's recorded painting result: display items in paint order, partitioned into chunks that share transform, clip, effect, and scroll property state. PaintArtifactCompositor converts it into compositor layers and property trees.

title: Paint Invalidation
definition: Paint invalidation identifies recorded drawing that can no longer be reused after content or geometry changes. Fine-grained invalidation allows unchanged display items and subsequences to remain cached, reducing the work needed for the next frame.

title: Property Trees
definition: Property trees represent transforms, clips, visual effects, and scrolling independently from the DOM and layout trees. Sharing and referencing these nodes lets the compositor update many visual changes without rebuilding or repainting all content.

title: Compositing
definition: Compositing decides how painted content becomes layers and combines those layers into frames. Separating layers can let scrolling, transforms, and animations update on the compositor thread without rerunning the entire Blink lifecycle.

title: Rasterization
definition: Rasterization executes recorded paint operations to produce pixel tiles, often using GPU acceleration. Chromium prioritizes visible tiles, schedules raster work, and uploads or retains resources so the compositor can assemble a frame quickly.

title: Viz
definition: Viz is Chromium's display compositor service. It receives compositor frames from renderers and browser UI, aggregates surfaces, performs final drawing, and presents the result through the platform display pipeline.

title: Surface and CompositorFrame
definition: A CompositorFrame packages render passes and resources submitted to Viz, while a Surface is the retained slot where that frame participates in aggregation. Surface identifiers let content embedded across processes reference the correct evolving visual output.

title: BeginFrame
definition: BeginFrame signals tell producers when to update visual state for an upcoming display frame. The cadence flows from display timing through Viz and compositor scheduling toward renderers, coordinating animation and rendering work around vsync.

title: GPU Process
definition: The GPU process isolates graphics-driver interaction and executes validated graphics commands for Chromium clients. It supports raster, compositing, WebGL/WebGPU, and video paths while keeping unstable or privileged driver access outside renderers.

title: Ozone
definition: Ozone is Chromium's abstraction between higher-level UI and graphics code and platform window systems. Platform backends supply surfaces, input, cursors, displays, and GPU integration without forcing the rest of Chromium to depend directly on X11, Wayland, DRM, or other native APIs.

title: V8
definition: V8 is the JavaScript and WebAssembly engine embedded by Chromium. It parses and compiles code, executes it inside isolates and contexts, manages JavaScript memory, and connects to Blink's DOM objects through generated bindings.

title: Isolate and Context
definition: A V8 isolate is an independent JavaScript heap and runtime instance; a context is a global execution environment inside an isolate. Chromium commonly shares an isolate on a renderer thread while using contexts and security checks to represent different worlds or documents.

title: Blink–V8 Bindings
definition: Blink bindings expose Web IDL interfaces such as Document and Element as JavaScript objects managed by V8. Generated glue converts values, checks contexts and security, and keeps wrapper lifetimes coordinated with Blink's garbage-collected objects.

title: Tasks, Threads, and Sequences
definition: Chromium schedules units of work as tasks through sequenced task runners rather than encouraging arbitrary thread access. A sequence guarantees ordering without necessarily pinning every task to one physical thread, and callbacks carry results back across boundaries.

title: Event Loop
definition: A renderer main thread repeatedly runs queued tasks, drains microtasks at specified checkpoints, and participates in rendering opportunities. Long JavaScript tasks delay input, lifecycle updates, and presentation because these responsibilities share the same event-loop thread.

title: Workers
definition: Dedicated, shared, and service workers run web scripts outside a document's main thread, with different ownership and lifetime rules. Chromium connects browser-side hosts to Blink worker threads and assigns processes under the same site and security constraints used elsewhere.

title: Garbage Collection (Oilpan + V8)
definition: V8 collects JavaScript objects while Blink's Oilpan collector manages many C++ DOM objects. Unified heap integration traces relationships across the JavaScript/C++ boundary so wrappers and their native objects stay alive exactly while reachable.

title: Sandbox and the Rule of Two
definition: Chromium sandboxes processes that handle untrustworthy content, restricting direct access to files, devices, and powerful operating-system APIs. The Rule of Two says code should not simultaneously handle untrustworthy input, be memory-unsafe, and hold high privilege; architecture should eliminate at least one of those three conditions.

title: Tracing
definition: Tracing records timestamped events, counters, and flows from Chromium's many threads and processes into a unified performance timeline. Perfetto-compatible traces let developers follow work such as navigation, scheduling, rendering, and memory activity across subsystem boundaries rather than guessing from a single stack trace.
